source_name: ЈП Градски паркинг Скопје / Parking.MK app coverage
why_relevant: Documents the four parking payment channels in Skopje (card-in-app, SMS, QR, scratch cards) and the municipal parking operators (JP Gradski parking, Parkinzi na Opstina Centar / POC) — a clean, measurable micro-payments acceptance segment and a candidate for card-vs-SMS substitution tracking.

source_name: CaSys International (casys.com.mk) — processor site & blog
why_relevant: The dominant MK card processor sits behind most merchant checkouts and ATM/POS estates; its site, client references and blog posts are the fastest route to mapping which merchants and banks are on which rails — the supplier-side mirror of the merchant payment pages.

source_name: CaSys c-Pay (cpay.com.mk) — e-commerce gateway
why_relevant: The gateway host MK webshops redirect to at checkout; its documentation and feature pages (PayByLink, merchant portal, risk lists) define what MK online merchants can offer, and its hostname in checkout redirects is a machine-detectable fingerprint for gateway share.

source_name: Monri Payments Северна Македонија (monri.mk / monri.com/mk/webpay)
why_relevant: Regional PSP actively selling into MK e-commerce; its product and integration pages list supported platforms (WooCommerce, Magento, PrestaShop, OpenCart) and named reservation-system partners, revealing competitive entry against CaSys and which merchant verticals are being won.

source_name: Стопанска банка — Купување на рати без камата (merchant partner list)
why_relevant: Bank-published lists of interest-free instalment partner merchants are effectively a published acceptance/merchant roster per bank — the closest public proxy to acquiring relationships and merchant-category coverage in MK.

source_name: Комерцијална банка — Плаќање на рати без камата (merchant partner list)
why_relevant: Second major bank's published instalment-merchant roster; cross-referencing rosters across banks yields an approximate merchant-by-acquirer map for large MK chains.

source_name: Makpetrol — Верна / Vera loyalty and fuel payment cards
why_relevant: The largest MK fuel retailer's closed-loop payment/loyalty card programme (Vera, Vera+ business cards) — closed-loop fuel cards are a direct substitute for card acceptance volume at forecourts and a marker of the acceptance mix at a high-frequency merchant category.

source_name: Lukoil Macedonia — LUKOIL Club card / mobile app listing
why_relevant: App-store listing for the second major fuel chain's card/app programme; release notes are a cheap, dated change-feed for added payment features (in-app pay, contactless, wallet support) at fuel forecourts.

source_name: bne IntelliNews — Nayax and MK cashless acceptance (unattended payments)
why_relevant: Regional business press covering foreign acceptance-technology entrants (Nayax) into MK unattended payments — vending, parking, EV charging — a segment no MK regulator breaks out and a leading indicator of terminal-estate growth.

source_name: Netcetera — Halkbank North Macedonia wallet reference case
why_relevant: Vendor reference/case-study pages are one of the few places where MK bank–supplier contracts for wallets, 3DS and contactless are named publicly; supplier reference libraries are a systematic route to the acceptance technology stack.

source_name: Google Wallet — supported payment methods, North Macedonia
why_relevant: Scheme/wallet operator's own country page enumerating which MK banks and card products are enabled for Google Wallet — an authoritative, regularly updated issuer list that maps digital-wallet acceptance readiness; the Apple Pay equivalent should be tracked alongside.

source_name: Wikipedia — List of supermarket chains in North Macedonia
why_relevant: Cheap seed roster of the large grocery chains (Tinex, Vero, KAM, Ramstore, Stokomak et al.) needed to build the merchant-acceptance census; each entry snowballs to a corporate site, payment page and store count.

source_name: Faktor.mk — toll tariffs and payment-method explainers
why_relevant: MK business outlet that publishes practical explainers enumerating which payment instruments are accepted at toll plazas (cash, bank cards, contactless smart cards) — useful where the road operator (ЈПДП) publishes sparsely.

source_name: IT.mk forum — merchant threads on CaSys / e-commerce onboarding
why_relevant: Practitioner forum where MK merchants and developers discuss acquirer onboarding, fees, gateway integration pain and alternatives — an unusually candid, otherwise unpublished view of merchant-side pricing and friction.

source_name: НБРСМ — Регистар на институции за електронски пари (E-money institution register)
why_relevant: Statutory public register of licensed e-money institutions maintained by the central bank under the Law on Payment Services and Payment Systems; each entry is a dated authorisation event and a pointer to a non-bank payment player that would otherwise be invisible.

source_name: НБРСМ — Издавање дозволи (licensing procedure for PI/EMI)
why_relevant: Documents the authorisation pathway, required documentation and contact channel (licenciranjepups@nbrm.mk) for payment institutions / EMIs; useful for interpreting register changes and for gauging barriers to entry.

source_name: НБРСМ — Подзаконски акти од Законот за платежни услуги и платни системи (bylaws under the PSPS Law)
why_relevant: Consolidated list of every NBRSM decision/instruction implementing the PSD2-aligned law — including the Decision on issuing licences and consents to PIs/EMIs and on the content and manner of keeping the registers. Dated regulatory events, the core of this cell.

source_name: НБРСМ — Закон за платежни услуги и платни системи (law landing page)
why_relevant: Central bank's canonical page for the PSD2-transposing law (Official Gazette RSM 90/22, in force 1 Jan 2023), with links to amendments and the unofficial consolidated text.

source_name: НБРСМ — unofficial consolidated text of the PSPS Law (PDF, 144-25)
why_relevant: Full current statutory text including register provisions, interchange/'заменски надоместок' definitions and fee-transparency rules; the filename suffix (144-25) signals the latest amending Gazette issue, making version tracking easy.

source_name: ЕНЕР — Единствен национален електронски регистар на прописи (draft-law consultation portal)
why_relevant: Government's mandatory pre-adoption consultation register. Draft payment-services and FX laws appear here with regulatory impact assessments months before Official Gazette publication — the earliest lead indicator of regulatory change. Item 57347 is the PSPS draft law; item 77045 the FX-law alignment amendment.

source_name: Службен весник на РСМ (Official Gazette of North Macedonia)
why_relevant: Legal source of record. The PSPS Law is Official Gazette RSM No. 90/22 (in force 1 Jan 2023) with later amendments; every NBRSM decision on licensing, registers and fees is dated by its Gazette issue. Authoritative for the 'when' of every regulatory event.

source_name: Министерство за финансии — portal.mdt.gov.mk consolidated financial-system laws compendium
why_relevant: Government-published compendium of the laws governing the financial system, containing the editorially consolidated PSPS Law text. Useful as a non-bot-defended mirror when nbrm.mk blocks, and as evidence of Ministry-of-Finance policy ownership.

source_name: НБРСМ mirror of the AML/CFT Law (Закон за спречување перење пари и финансирање тероризам, консолидиран текст)
why_relevant: Consolidated AML law text as maintained for supervised financial institutions; contains the cash-transaction thresholds and reporting duties that bear directly on cash usage measurement.

source_name: European Payments Council — Register of Participants in SEPA schemes
why_relevant: North Macedonia entered the SEPA schemes' geographical scope on 6 March 2025; adherence opened April 2025 with an Operational Readiness Date of 5 October 2025, and the first MK banks are registered in SCT. The register names each adhering MK PSP and which schemes (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD) it joined — a dated, machine-readable indicator of instant-payments readiness at institution level.

source_name: European Commission — North Macedonia Enlargement Report (SWD(2025) 753 final) and enlargement newsroom
why_relevant: Annual, dated third-party assessment of alignment with the payments acquis (Chapter 4 free movement of capital, Chapter 9 financial services): notes PSD2 transposition status, SEPA accession March 2025, and remaining gaps. Excellent independent cross-check on NBRSM self-reporting and a reliable annual cadence.

source_name: Програма на економски реформи 2025-2027 (Economic Reform Programme, Ministry of Finance)
why_relevant: Government's forward-looking reform commitments to the EU, which typically carry dated milestones for payments reform (instant payments, SEPA, digitalisation of payments, cash-economy measures). Gives intended timelines that can be tested against actual regulatory events.

source_name: НБРСМ Конференција за плаќањата и пазарната инфраструктура (payments & market infrastructure conference)
why_relevant: Biennial/annual NBRSM conference where instant-payments plans, interchange policy and licensing outcomes are first articulated publicly by the Payment Systems Department; presentations often contain numbers not otherwise published.

source_name: Central Bank Payments News — interview with Igor Velickovski, Manager, Payment Systems Department, NBRSM
why_relevant: Named-source interview establishing the responsible NBRSM department and official for payment systems, plus stated intentions on instant payments and PSD2 implementation. Useful for the actor map and for attributing later statements.
